collections.name: TAPUHI

baseline.method: BROKEN: 5-step NDHA resolve -> weserv proxy of the FL stream, but the FL stream is JP2 and weserv can't decode JP2 -> HTTP 404 for every record
baseline.px: 404 (broken); harvested NLNZStreamGate IE access copy is ~700px JPEG

chosen.method: tapuhiConverter strategy: resolve IE -> Rosetta METS (dps_func=mets, stateless GET) -> pick the largest image/jp2 file (<=100MB) from the METS file list -> return <Jp2ConverterFnUrl>/?url=<encoded FL stream>. (The METS replaced the old DVS+ieViewer HTML scrape, which omitted the FL PIDs for ~60%+ of records -> raised the converter hit rate from ~37% to ~93%.) Converter is a self-hosted Python+Pillow JP2->JPEG Lambda (container image, arm64 2048MB/60s, Function URL, host-allowlisted to ndhadeliver.natlib.govt.nz) deployed with the Swift Lambda under one AWS SAM stack; JP2_CONVERTER_URL injected via !GetAtt. Pillow decodes a REDUCED JP2 resolution level (image.reduce, wavelet) sized just above MAX_DIM so 50-70MP masters decode in seconds not ~30s; keeps grayscale L; downscales long side <=4000 under the 6 MB Function URL base64 cap. Graceful fallback to the 700px NLNZStreamGate access copy if the resolve throws or JP2_CONVERTER_URL is unset (never weserv, never raw JP2).
chosen.px: JP2 master -> JPEG via converter; verified LIVE up to 4000px from 48-69MP masters (e.g. FL13222808 8088x5956, FL32545377 9279x7487); ~93% converter hit rate; 700px NLNZStreamGate fallback for the rest

collections.notes: DONE: self-hosted Python+Pillow JP2->JPEG converter Lambda built + deployed with the Swift Lambda under one AWS SAM stack (template.yaml, Makefile, converter/{app.py,Dockerfile,requirements.txt}). Build-time HARD-ASSERT features.check('jpg_2000'). Swift wired via tapuhiConverter strategy in URLProcessor.swift (legacy switch case removed; registry entry added). FOLLOW-UP FIX (2026-06-09): replaced the resolve's DVS+ieViewer HTML scrape (fragile, session-dependent; missed FL PIDs for ~60%+ of records -> ~37% converter hit rate) with a stateless Rosetta METS parse (largestTapuhiJP2PID picks the largest image/jp2 <=100MB) -> ~93% hit rate; and added a JP2 reduced-resolution decode (image.reduce) + raised converter to 2048MB/60s + download cap 110MB so 48-69MP masters that previously TIMED OUT (~30s -> 502) now convert in seconds. Verified LIVE on AWS (stack 'nzimageapi', ap-southeast-2): converter returns image/jpeg, RENDERS IN CHROME, guards 400/403; deployed /image?collection=TAPUHI -> 14/15 converter URLs. Per-request latency split (instrumented): ~4s total for ~6MB masters, ~9-19s for 15-64MB masters (download from NDHA's Rosetta servlet ~1-16s + Pillow reduced decode/encode ~2-10s; memory fine at 274MB used). User declined caching (rare cache hits for a random-image API) and accepted the on-demand latency. CUTOVER PENDING: SAM created a NEW HTTP API endpoint (ImageApiEndpoint) + converter Function URL; old hand-made function + scripts/*.sh kept as rollback until clients repointed. thumbnailer.digitalnz.org still DEAD (NXDOMAIN) -> thumbnailerProxy helper still unreferenced (final-cleanup note). Sweep resumes at order 26 (Canterbury Museum) -- NOT started.

collections.notes: PLATFORM CORRECTED: Vernon CMS (Vernon Systems, the eHive vendor) -- NOT eMuseum. Detected via the 404 page's vernon-common.min.js/vernon-shortlist.min.js (object pages are AWS-WAF-challenged, HTTP 202 x-amzn-waf-action=challenge -> uncrawlable by curl/Lambda/Wayback). Images on S3+CloudFront /records/images/<size>/<dir>/<sha1>.jpg. Full Vernon token ladder probed: nano(35)/tiny(75)/small(150)/medium(400)/large(800)/xlarge(~1000-1200) return 200; display/thumbnail/original/master/full/zoom/xxlarge all S3 403 AccessDenied (uniform across 5 records -> NOT rights-dependent). No public IIIF (/apis/iiif + /iiif 404 uniform), no OpenSeadragon/zoom reachable, no alternate hi-res host (object_url null), Wayback CDX empty (WAF blocks the crawler). CORRECTION: an earlier 'paid-only originals' claim (from a web-research subagent) is WITHDRAWN -- the museum image-service page (verified directly) says copies can be ORDERED from the Image Service and that photos 'can be downloaded from Collections Online'; it publishes NO fee/charge/price wording. RESOLVED GAP: user confirmed in-browser (2026-06-10) the WAF-walled object page's 'download from Collections Online' control serves xlarge as the highest -> xlarge is the genuine public ceiling. Harvested large_thumbnail_url is uniformly the /large/ form (10/10) so the swap always applies; xlarge is honest (no upscaling -> ==large for sub-800px originals, 1.5-2.25x for bigger). CONCLUSION: current shipped large->xlarge is already optimal = no-improvement. Left in legacy switch (precedent: Tamiro/Antarctica no-improvement collections stay in the switch); replacingOccurrences(of:large,to:xlarge) is safe for Canterbury (one occurrence, hex hash, fixed host).
